root_cause.text: In the `spi-fsl-spi` driver, the `fsl_spi_prepare_message` function switches to 16-bit mode for large transfers without verifying length parity, causing buffer overruns when odd-sized data is processed.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states the driver "failed to make sure that the size is really even before switching to 16 bit mode," which led to a "buffer overrun... when that size is odd," and the patch diff confirms the fix by adding the `!(t->len & 1)` condition to the length check in `fsl_spi_prepare_message`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `fsl_spi_prepare_message` function in the `spi-fsl-spi` driver enables 16-bit transfer mode without verifying that the transfer length is even, causing buffer overruns when odd-length transfers are processed with 16-bit hardware alignment expectations.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds the condition `!(t->len & 1)` to the `if` statement in `drivers/spi/spi-fsl-spi.c` that sets `t->bits_per_word = 16`, addressing the CVE description which states the driver "failed to make sure that the size is really even before switching to 16 bit mode" leading to buffer overruns with dynamically allocated bounce buffers.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `fsl_spi_prepare_message` function in the `spi-fsl-spi` driver enables 16-bit mode for transfers without validating that the length is even, causing a buffer overrun when odd-sized buffers are processed.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds the `!(t->len & 1)` check to the conditional statement in `drivers/spi/spi-fsl-spi.c` that determines whether to set `t->bits_per_word = 16`, fixing the omission noted in the CVE description where commit `fc96ec826bce` "failed to make sure that the size is really even before switching to 16 bit mode."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes CPM1 SPI configuration by restricting 16-bit mode usage to even-length transfers only.
intent_record.what: Inserted the condition `!(t->len & 1)` into the `if` statement that determines whether to set `t->bits_per_word` to 16.
intent_record.how: Prevents the driver from switching to 16-bit word mode for odd-length transfers on CPM1 hardware, forcing them to remain in 8-bit mode to avoid hardware incompatibility.
